answer.rationale: p99 latency is climbing on the write path during peak settlement traffic. The security patch cannot be reverted per compliance. Routing read queries to replicas (memory_b5 precedent) reduces load on the primary write path without reverting the release. This preserves the compliance-required patch, protects write throughput during peak load, and has prior success record. Verification of memory_b5 confirms this pattern resolved similar latency under write pressure. Regional failover risks moving the load to an equally constrained region during peak. Circuit breakers address failure modes, not capacity. Adding capacity takes time we don't have in this window.
